title: Critic's Eye: Review-Grounded Graph Reasoning for Long-Form Motif Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2610.35011v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep narrative understanding requires distinguishing what happens from how it is presented, moving beyond the chronological fabula to decode the sjuzet, the discursive organization through which themes are staged. We study this through the recurrence of literary motifs (blood in Macbeth, for instance), where symbolic significance emerges not from local cues, but through repetition-with-variation across the whole work. We operationalize this setting as Computational Motif Discovery, a transductive task that predicts missing line-motif links using the full narrative structure of a play. We propose Critic's Eye, which models the work as a heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graph and performs discriminative inference over global structural evidence. translated_title: 批评家之眼：基于评论的图推理用于长篇母题发现
translated_abstract: 深层的叙事理解需要区分“发生了什么”与“如何呈现”，即超越按时间顺序排列的故事情节，去解码情节组织——也就是主题得以展现的话语组织方式。我们通过文学母题的复现（例如《麦克白》中的“血”）来研究这一问题，其象征意义并非来自局部线索，而是通过贯穿全篇的变奏式重复得以显现。我们将这一设定形式化为计算母题发现，这是一个直推式任务，利用剧本的完整叙事结构来预测缺失的台词-母题关联。我们提出Critic's Eye（批评家之眼），它将作品建模为异构的叙事拓扑图，并在全局结构证据上进行判别式推理。Critic's Eye在我们的基准测试上达到84.8%的Hit@5，几乎是最新专有基础模型（Gemini-3-pro-preview，约22.6%）性能的四倍。我们的分析显示，尽管大规模……（原文在此截断）
tldr: 提出Critic's Eye方法，将文学作品建模为异构叙事拓扑图并基于全局结构证据进行判别式推理以发现文学母题，在基准测试上达到84.8%的Hit@5，约为顶尖专有大模型性能的四倍。
en_tdlr: Critic's Eye models literary works as heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graphs and performs discriminative inference over global structural evidence for computational motif discovery, achieving 84.8% Hit@5—nearly quadrupling the performance of state-of-the-art proprietary foundation models.
